description: Human-specific vs chimp-specific substitution scan against mammalian consensus, and hydropathy of the type-II signal anchor
code:
import json, numpy as np, pandas as pd, collections
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
D=json.load(open("gt6_panel.json")); seqs=D["seqs"]
maps=json.load(open("human_to_ortholog_maps.json"))
maps={o:{int(k):v for k,v in m.items()} for o,m in maps.items()}
H=seqs["A3GALT2_HUMAN"]
nonhom=["A3GALT2_RAT","A3GALT2_MOUSE","A3GALT2_MACAQUE","A3GALT2_MARMOSET","A3GALT2_DOG",
        "A3GALT2_CAT","A3GALT2_HORSE","A3GALT2_CAMEL","A3GALT2_NMRAT","A3GALT2_GPIG"]
chimp="A3GALT2_CHIMP"

rows=[]
for p in range(1,len(H)+1):
    col=[]
    for o in nonhom:
        q=maps[o].get(p)
        col.append(seqs[o][q-1] if q else "-")
    cons,ncons=collections.Counter([c for c in col if c!="-"]).most_common(1)[0]
    n=len([c for c in col if c!="-"])
    qc=maps[chimp].get(p); chres=seqs[chimp][qc-1] if qc else "-"
    rows.append(dict(pos=p,human=H[p-1],chimp=chres,consensus=cons,cons_frac=ncons/n,
                     n_orth=n,col="".join(col)))
df=pd.DataFrame(rows)
# strictly human-specific: human != consensus held by >=90% of non-hominids, AND chimp == consensus
hs = df[(df.human!=df.consensus)&(df.cons_frac>=0.9)&(df.chimp==df.consensus)]
# hominid-specific: human==chimp but both differ from a >=90% non-hominid consensus
hom = df[(df.human!=df.consensus)&(df.cons_frac>=0.9)&(df.chimp==df.human)]
# chimp-specific (control, same criteria applied to chimp)
cs = df[(df.chimp!=df.consensus)&(df.cons_frac>=0.9)&(df.human==df.consensus)]
print(f"Strictly human-specific substitutions (vs >=90% mammalian consensus): n={len(hs)}")
print(hs[['pos','human','consensus','cons_frac','n_orth']].to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nChimp-specific substitutions, same criteria (lineage control): n={len(cs)}")
print(cs[['pos','chimp','consensus','cons_frac']].to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nHominid-shared substitutions (human==chimp != consensus): n={len(hom)}")
print(hom[['pos','human','consensus','cons_frac']].to_string(index=False))

cat_pos=[108,109,110,111,112,113,199,200,201,221,222,223,224,233,291,333,334,335,336,337,338,339]
print("\nHuman-specific subs at GT6 catalytic/donor positions:", sorted(set(hs.pos)&set(cat_pos)))
print("Hominid-shared subs at GT6 catalytic/donor positions:", sorted(set(hom.pos)&set(cat_pos)))

# ---- Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy for predicted type-II signal anchor, human vs rat ----
KD=dict(A=1.8,R=-4.5,N=-3.5,D=-3.5,C=2.5,Q=-3.5,E=-3.5,G=-0.4,H=-3.2,I=4.5,L=3.8,K=-3.9,
        M=1.9,F=2.8,P=-1.6,S=-0.8,T=-0.7,W=-0.9,Y=-1.3,V=4.2)
def kd(seq,w=19):
    v=[KD.get(c,0) for c in seq]
    return np.array([np.mean(v[max(0,i-w//2):i+w//2+1]) for i in range(len(v))])
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(13,4.2))
for nm,c in [("A3GALT2_HUMAN","#2d6cdf"),("A3GALT2_RAT","#d1495b"),("A3GALT2_MOUSE","#8a8a8a")]:
    s=seqs[nm]; ax[0].plot(range(1,len(s)+1),kd(s),label=nm.replace("A3GALT2_",""),color=c,lw=1.4)
ax[0].axhline(1.6,ls="--",c="k",lw=.8); ax[0].axvspan(13,32,color="orange",alpha=.25)
ax[0].set_xlim(0,80); ax[0].set_xlabel("residue"); ax[0].set_ylabel("Kyte-Doolittle (window 19)")
ax[0].set_title("N-terminal signal anchor region\norange = UniProt TM 13-32 (human)"); ax[0].legend(fontsize=8)
# panel 2: positions of human-specific subs along the protein with catalytic sites marked
ax[1].scatter(hs.pos,[1]*len(hs),marker="v",color="#d1495b",s=60,label=f"human-specific (n={len(hs)})")
ax[1].scatter(cs.pos,[0.8]*len(cs),marker="v",color="#999",s=50,label=f"chimp-specific (n={len(cs)})")
ax[1].scatter(cat_pos,[0.6]*len(cat_pos),marker="|",color="#2d6cdf",s=250,label="GT6 catalytic/donor sites")
ax[1].scatter([199,201,291],[0.6]*3,marker="o",color="#1a9850",s=55,zorder=5,label="DVD + catalytic Glu")
ax[1].set_ylim(0.4,1.3); ax[1].set_yticks([]); ax[1].set_xlabel("human A3GALT2 residue")
ax[1].set_xlim(0,345); ax[1].legend(fontsize=8,loc="upper center",ncol=2)
ax[1].set_title("Lineage-specific substitutions vs catalytic machinery")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
df.to_csv("per_position_consensus.csv",index=False)
hs.to_csv("human_specific_subs.csv",index=False)
